events.subtitle: Experimental flute, improvisation and electronic listening practices
events.factual_description: Rhizome DC presents Wilfrido Terrazas and Rachel Beetz on Wednesday, September 2, 2026, with the event beginning at 19:00 at 6950 Maple Street NW, Washington, DC. The official venue page and its authorized Pools ticket page list a $10-$25 sliding-scale ticket; Pools separately displays fee-inclusive totals of $11.91-$27.75. Rhizome identifies Terrazas as a flutist, improviser, composer and educator from Ensenada, Mexico, whose work connects notation, improvisation, experimental lineages, Mexican folk traditions and poetry. The same primary listing describes Beetz as a composer, flutist and improviser whose practice combines field recordings and electronically modified flutes. The page bills both artists for the evening but does not specify a duo format, set order, doors time, or additional personnel, so none are inferred here.

The source does not publish a duo claim, set order, doors time or additional personnel, and none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: The bill puts two very different flute-centered experimental languages in the same room. Terrazas works between notation, open improvisation, Mexican musical memory and poetry; Beetz turns flutes, electronics and environmental listening into slowly shifting sound environments. The connection is the instrument, but the attraction is hearing how differently each artist makes it behave.
en.trip_verdict: If Wednesday is free in the DMV, this is worth catching at Rhizome, especially for the instrumental and improvisational thread. It is a focused local discovery rather than a reason to reorganize a larger regional itinerary.
en.listen_before: Wilfrido Terrazas — My Shadow Leads the Way; Rachel Beetz — Unofficial

es.why_it_matters: El cartel pone en la misma sala dos lenguajes experimentales muy distintos construidos alrededor de la flauta. Terrazas trabaja entre notación, improvisación abierta, memoria musical mexicana y poesía; Beetz convierte flautas, electrónica y escucha ambiental en espacios sonoros que cambian lentamente. El punto de contacto es el instrumento, pero lo interesante es escuchar hasta dónde lo lleva cada uno.
es.trip_verdict: Si el miércoles está libre en el DMV, vale caer a Rhizome, sobre todo por el hilo instrumental e improvisatorio. Es un descubrimiento local bien enfocado, no una razón para reorganizar un itinerario regional más grande.
es.listen_before: Wilfrido Terrazas — My Shadow Leads the Way; Rachel Beetz — Unofficial
